newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - OECD votes to admit South Korea.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - OECD votes to admit South Korea.

text.p: South Korea got the green light on Friday to join the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development as first Asian member besides economic superpower Japan in the club of the world's economic establishment.

It will enter hot on the heels of Poland, the latest in a long line of emerging economies to join an organisation that was once the reserve of richer nations but now embraces an increasing number who sign up to its free-market principles.

South Korean foreign minister Gong Ro-myung will attend a ceremony with OECD secretary general Donald Johnson in Paris on October 25 marking the invitation of South Korea to become the 29th member of the organisation, the OECD said in a statement.
"The economic development of the Republic of Korea over the past 30 years has been among the most rapid and sustained in the world," the OECD said.

South Korea would be the 11th largest exporter in the OECD zone and accounted for about 2.5 percent of world exports, a position which had been enhanced through liberalisation of its own import controls, the OECD statement said.

"Moreover, the size of the public sector is amongst the smallest in the OECD area," it said, adding that successful education programmes had helped to keep the unemployment rate -- two percent in 1995 -- at the lowest in the OECD.
From the wider Asia-Pacific area, Australia and New Zealand are also members of the OECD.
South Korea will become a member once it ratifies the OECD convention and goes through the formal procedures of lodging it with the French government, the depositary of the convention.
In the meantime, South Korea will be able to participate in OECD's work as an observer, the OECD said.
In order to be accepted into the OECD, South Korea had to prove it was liberalising its services and financial markets sectors to comply with OECD free market rules.
Some OECD members, such as relative newcomer Hungary, see the organisation very much as a symbol of economic credibility and a stepping stone to membership of the European Union.
Slovakia is also waiting in the wings and Russia said last May it was interested in joining.
